name: Dianzani Autoimmune Lymphoproliferative Disease

criteria.description: Persistent, non-malignant lymphadenopathy lasting more than 6 months
Presence of autoimmune cytopenias such as autoimmune hemolytic anemia or thrombocytopenia
Elevated levels of polyclonal immunoglobulins in serum
Exclusion of malignant lymphoproliferative disorders by biopsy and clinical evaluation
Lymph node biopsy showing reactive hyperplasia without clonal proliferation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic lymphadenopathy, autoimmune hematologic manifestations, exclusion of malignancy, and supportive histopathologic findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including hematology, immunology, and pathology.

pathognomonic.notes: Persistent enlargement of lymph nodes without evidence of malignancy
Destruction of red blood cells mediated by autoantibodies
searchTerms: immune system destroying red blood cells
red blood cell breakdown from antibodies

common.symptomName: Thrombocytopenia due to autoimmune platelet destruction
common.notes: Low platelet counts leading to bleeding tendencies
searchTerms: low platelet count from immune attack

common.notes: Elevated immunoglobulin levels reflecting immune activation
Enlarged spleen due to lymphoid proliferation
Increased susceptibility due to immune dysregulation

occasional.notes: Enlarged liver associated with lymphoid infiltration
Low neutrophil counts caused by autoantibodies

rare.notes: Inflammation of small blood vessels in the skin

laboratory: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia evidenced by positive direct Coombs test
Polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia on serum protein electrophoresis
imaging: Ultrasound or CT showing lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; diagnosis is clinical and histopathologic
other: Lymph node biopsy showing reactive hyperplasia without clonal lymphoid proliferation

distinguishingFeatures: ALPS typically presents with elevated double-negative T cells and FAS gene mutations
More frequent autoimmune cytopenias and lymphoma risk
Presence of Reed-Sternberg cells on lymph node biopsy

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging lymph nodes suggestive of malignancy
Severe autoimmune cytopenias causing life-threatening bleeding or anemia
Development of lymphoma or other malignancies
references: Dianzani U, et al. Autoimmune lymphoproliferative disease: clinical and pathological features. J Clin Pathol. 1980.
Orphanet: Dianzani autoimmune lymphoproliferative disease. ORPHA:275523.
Fischer A, et al. Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndromes: pathophysiology and treatment. Blood. 2017.
